conventions.convention: Continuous compactly supported top forms on oriented boundaryless four-manifolds are integrated by finite positive-chart cutoff sums of Riemann integrals. Countable Choice is retained for compatibility with the earlier smooth integral.
The metric has signature (-,+,+,+), the orientation is independent of time orientation, X=-F_ab F^ab/4, Y=-F_ab (star F)^ab/4, and H^ab=L_X F^ab+L_Y (star F)^ab.

Variations add a smooth compactly supported global physical-potential one-form to all local representatives in one fixed bundle sector, giving F_epsilon=F+epsilon da. Stationarity concerns the relative action difference, without requiring a finite unvaried action.
L is C² on all of R²; H is C¹ and its divergence is continuous. The normalization L=X has no SI action prefactor or assigned QED coefficient.

Contract-admissibility requires, for every supplied state, divergence j=0 and ∇^a T_ab=F_bc j^c. The sourced Maxwell sign is ∇_a F^ab=-mu_0 j^b; the classical electromagnetic stress has the opposite exchange divergence.

The semiclassical consistency deduction assumes smooth fields, constant mu_0>0, constant kappa≠0, and constant Lambda. It establishes necessary identities, without constructing quantum states or renormalized sources.

The counterexample uses length coordinates (t,x,y,z), dimensionless epsilon∈(0,1), fixed positive field and length scales, and arbitrary fixed finite alpha,beta. Its exact fields are configurations, without an asserted field equation.

load_bearing.statement: The finite positive-chart cutoff formula defines a linear, local integral for continuous compactly supported real top forms on an oriented smooth Hausdorff second-countable boundaryless four-manifold, independent of charts, cutoffs and bounding rectangles, compatible with the earlier smooth integral and continuous under uniform convergence of finitely many fixed chart coefficients.

On a fixed smooth Lorentzian geometry and circle-bundle connection sector, define X=-F_ab F^ab/4, Y=-F_ab (star F)^ab/4, L∈C²(R²), and H^ab=L_X F^ab+L_Y (star F)^ab. Compact global physical-potential variations give F_epsilon=F+epsilon da; stationarity differentiates the continuous compact-support relative action.

If the connection in the fixed-metric, fixed-bundle-sector C² Lagrangian model is stationary under every permitted compact variation and source coupling is absent, then ∇_a H^ab=0 and dF=0. For L=X+alpha X²+beta Y², H^ab=(1+2alpha X)F^ab+2beta Y(star F)^ab.

For supplied algebra, state class, renormalization prescription and smooth source maps, contract-admissibility means that every supplied state satisfies ∇_a j_R^a=0 and ∇^a T_R,ab=F_bc j_R^c. This is a predicate on candidate data, without an existence assertion.
For smooth fields and constants mu_0>0, kappa≠0 and Lambda, the equations dF=0, ∇_a F^ab=-mu_0 j^b and G_ab+Lambda g_ab=kappa(T_EM,ab+T_ren,ab) imply ∇_a j^a=0 and ∇^a T_ren,ab=F_bc j^c.

concerns.concern: The first Remarks paragraph says: “A source-free nonlinear constitutive equation is a model distinct from linear Maxwell unless L=X (up to an overall constant).” As a necessary criterion for obtaining the Maxwell equation this is overstrong. L=X+C has exactly the same relative action and H=F. More substantially, L=X+theta Y with constant theta gives H=F+theta star F, and dF=0 implies ∇_a(star F)^ab=0, so its source-free equation is again the Maxwell equation. This concerns the closing remark, not the validity of the stated variation proposition.
